title: Introduce session-protocol v2 and ergonomic cancelable stream factory across SDKs
author: Lena Park
description:
Motivation: We have accumulated multiple ad-hoc session/reauth behaviors in the three SDKs that cause surprising reconnection patterns and duplicate heartbeats for long-lived streams. This PR introduces a harmonized session protocol v2 (wire-compatible fallback to v1) plus a small, ergonomic StreamFactory that produces cancelable async iterators/async generators across Python/TS/Go. Goals: 1) provide a single session lease/heartbeat contract that SDKs can rely on; 2) centralize adaptive reauth window logic and expose conservative defaults; 3) give application teams a simple cancelable iterator abstraction (with drain-on-cancel and optional graceful-finish) to reduce onboarding friction; 4) bump SDK versions with compat shims and add crosslang examples. Summary of changes (high level): - Add session-protocol v2 definitions and negotiation handshake in the client transport layer. v2 adds a lease_id and optional lease_ttl_jitter that servers can use for preferred refresh windows. Clients fall back to v1 when server does not support v2. - Introduce adaptive-reauth window: clients compute reauth_at = lease_expiry - min(max(lease_ttl * 0.15, 5s), 60s) and can apply a tunable jitter. This reduces simultaneous refresh storms. - New StreamFactory API in each SDK: Python: StreamFactory.cancelable_async_iter(stream_handle, on_cancel="drain" | "finish"); TypeScript: createCancelableAsyncIterator(stream, {onCancel}); Go: CancelableIterator wrapper with Context-cancellation integration. - Implement per-SDK compatibility shim that allows existing consumer patterns to keep working; new ergonomic patterns are opt-in. - Tighten telemetry: emit session.lease_acquired, session.lease_refreshed, session.lease_failed with attachable tags (sdk, version, region) and add counters for reauth_attempts and reauth_backoff_ms. - Tests: unit tests for handshake negotiation, simulated lease jitter, and cancel-on-cancel semantics; integration test fixture that runs a mock server that advertises v2. - Docs: cross-sdk example added to redwood-examples and API docs updated with migration notes. - Version bumps: py 1.8.0 -> 1.9.0, ts 1.27.0 -> 1.28.0, go 1.7.3 -> 1.8.0. Checklist: 
- [x] Cross-SDK API design review (ENG-2203)
- [x] Backwards compatibility shim in each SDK
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Telemetry added and validated in staging
- [x] Docs and examples updated
- [x] Release notes drafted Notes on compatibility and migration: The default behavior is backwards compatible; servers not advertising v2 continue to work. Teams that relied on manual heartbeat/resend loops should migrate to the StreamFactory cancel handlers to avoid duplicate drains. There is no expected breaking behavior, but SDK consumers that relied on implicit duplicated reauth calls in race windows may see fewer redundant refreshes (which is a correctness/perf win).

review_conversation:
Diego Alvarez: Can we reduce the default reauth window to 10% instead of 15%? Concern is early churn for very short leases.
Lena Park: I tried 10% initially; 15% gives more headroom for noisy networks and aligns with our current implicit behavior. Added jitter min/max guard to avoid extreme cases.
Maya Chen: The Python cancelable iterator API looks ergonomic but can we document how drain vs finish interacts with in-flight errors?
Lena Park: Added a paragraph in the docs and updated unit tests to assert that onCancel='finish' will drain pending chunks and then close the iterator with the last error preserved.
Omar Rahman: Telemetry tags look good; can we emit a boolean session.v2_supported tag once per process?
Diego Alvarez: LGTMed after small nits (renamed a test helper).
Maya Chen: Approved.
Outcome: Addressed all review comments; Diego requested one last CI run after test flakiness fix and then merged with squash merge.

SDK bumps: python 1.9.0, typescript 1.28.0, go 1.8.0. Backwards compatible; opt-in ergonomics for cancel behavior. See docs/sdk/session-protocol-v2.md for migration guidance.
notes_for_backport: No runtime or infra changes required. For maintenance releases (if backporting to 1.8.x), apply session_shim only and skip StreamFactory for SDKs where major version policy forbids API additions.
